changed.title: A fixed 128 by 128 graph given by its table: some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 1200 gates is right whenever one row and one column are on
changed.unlocks: how far below our own circuit this graph goes at 1200 gates, for the line on the unstruck rule's graph
changed.context: A search. A circuit one gate below our own construction for this graph is checked; we hold none of 1200 gates and none has been found; this is a search. Row u of the table, as a 128-bit hex number, is entry u of the list in the statement; bit v is set when row u is joined to column v. Answer with a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, each reading at most two wires) and its output wire: only the gate list is checked, on the 16384 inputs with one row and one column on. A prover can use lean/PEqualNP/Library/Helpers/PromiseColTree.lean.

changed.title: Binary encoder with negations on 16 one-hot inputs: some AND/OR circuit of at most 31 gates, fan-in at most two, has all 4 bit wires and all 4 negated ones
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 31 ∧ ∀ v : Fin 4, (∃ w : ℕ, ∀ p : Fin 16, (C.wires (List.ofFn (fun q : Fin 16 => decide (q = p)))).getD w false = Nat.testBit p.val v.val) ∧ (∃ w : ℕ, ∀ p : Fin 16, (C.wires (List.ofFn (fun q : Fin 16 => decide (q = p)))).getD w false = !(Nat.testBit p.val v.val))
changed.unlocks: a smaller circuit for the layer that turns one-hot inputs into index bits, which every representing bound of ours is measured against
changed.context: A calibration of our constructions; no claim attached either way. Answer with a gate list of AND and OR gates of fan-in two and the eight wires (four bits, four negated bits), judged on the 16 one-hot inputs. We hold 32 gates (computed): row and column ORs of the 4 by 4 index grid, then a 4-gate encoder on each four. Truth unknown to us. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 103928 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 11 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (103928 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 11
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 12 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 11; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 4. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.
